title: NVIDIA/OpenShell: a policy runtime for agent fleets
friendlyTitle: OpenShell lets an agent work inside a policy you set
summary: OpenShell is an Apache-2.0 runtime that puts each agent in a sandbox and enforces a policy on files, system calls, and network connections. Agents do not see real credentials. OpenShell adds them only to requests for approved endpoints, and it uses a formal check to flag a policy change that would grant new access before a person approves it. It runs on Linux, Apple Silicon, and experimental WSL 2. GitHub's daily trending list had it at 1,240 stars today. The repository has 18,661 stars.
friendlySummary: OpenShell is a runtime for fleets of agents. Each agent runs in a sandbox. A policy controls which files, system calls, and network connections it can use. The agent does not see real passwords or keys. OpenShell adds them only to requests for approved sites, and it flags a policy change that would grant new access before a person approves it. It runs on Linux, Apple Silicon, and experimental Windows WSL 2. GitHub's daily trending list had it at 1,240 stars today. The repository has 18,661 stars. The license is Apache-2.0.
whyItMatters: If an agent needs to install packages or call an API, this is a way to give it that reach without handing it your keys or an open network. You still have to write the policy. A default sandbox image does not include an agent. The 0.1.x line is the current release.
friendlyWhyItMatters: If an agent needs to install packages or call an API, this is a way to allow that without giving it your keys or an open network. You still have to write the rules. The default sandbox does not include an agent. The current release line is 0.1.x.
